To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified RUVBL1/RUVBL2 and the R2TP Complex as novel interactors and functional regulators of EBOV nucleo-protein.
we have identified RUVBL1/2 and the R2TP-complex as novel interactors and functional partners of the Ebola virus nucleoprotein.
we identified RUVBL1/2, components of the RUVBL1-RUVBL2-RPAP3-PIH1D1 complex, as novel EBOV NP interactors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of cellular interactors of the nucleoprotein (N) of the Ebola virus (EVO) and the elucidation of the role these interactors play in the viral life cycle of EVO.
the identification of novel host factors involved in EBOV NP-host interactions.
the identification of novel host-pathogen interactions of Ebola virus nucleoprotein.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have identified RUVBL1/2 as novel cellular interactors of EVOV NP and have provided the first evidence for NP recruitment of the cellular R2TP complex.
we have identified RUVBL1 as a novel cellular interactor of NP and that the R2TP-complex is involved in capsid formation.
we identified novel cellular interactors of EVOB NP, RUVBL1/2, which may provide a novel target for broad-acting antiviral therapeutics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified two novel cellular interactors for the EBOV NP, RUVBL1/2.

we identified two novel interactors, RUVBL1 & RUVBL2 of EBOV nucleocapsid protein (NP), which are part of the R2PT complex, and we also found that knockdown of RUBVL1, but not RUVB2, reduced EBOV minigene activity.
we have identified two novel cellular interactors of the EBOV NP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we identified novel host-pathogen interactions between the Ebola virus nucleoprotein and RUVBL1/2, partner proteins of the AAA+ superfamily, as well as the R2TP (RUVBL1/ RUVBL2-PIH1D1-RPAP3) complex.
we identified two new EBOV nucleotide protein (NP) cellular interactors RUVB1L and RUVB2L.
we identified RUVBL1/RUVBL2 as new host interactors of the Ebola virus nucleoprotein.
